notes: Part A justifications: (1) taxable temporary - Originates when GAAP records the full gross profit; reverses as cash is collected and the tax return picks the income up -> future taxable amounts.; (2) deductible temporary - Originates when the cash is taxed ahead of the book revenue; reverses when GAAP later earns the revenue with no further tax -> future deductible amounts.; (3) taxable temporary - Originates while the tax deduction exceeds book depreciation; reverses in the later years when book depreciation exceeds tax -> future taxable amounts.; (4) permanent (nontaxable) - Book gain is excluded from taxable income permanently -- never reverses.; (5) permanent (nondeductible) - Book expense is never deductible on the return -- never reverses.; (6) taxable temporary - Originates when GAAP marks the security up; reverses on sale when the gain enters taxable income -> future taxable amounts.; (7) deductible temporary - Originates when GAAP accrues the estimated liability; reverses when the cash is paid and the deduction is taken -> future deductible amounts.; (8) permanent (nondeductible) - Book interest expense is permanently disallowed on the return -- never reverses.; (9) no book-tax difference - Book and tax revenue are the same amount this year, so there is nothing to originate or reverse.; (10) deductible temporary - Originates when GAAP books the write-down; reverses when the inventory is sold and the loss becomes deductible -> future deductible amounts. | Part C effect in words: the warranty payment reverses $7,000 of the deductible temporary difference (from $18,000 to $11,000), so the related deferred tax asset falls by $1,750 (from $4,500 to $2,750) at the 25% rate. The settlement entry itself touches no tax account; the DTA change is picked up in the year's income tax provision entry.
